MetaMath.comment: Added B3 2026-08-09 (AD-Gacha, Lobby). The algorithms the blueprint says to implement ONCE for every meta system: Slot(period, offsetSec) deterministic time buckets (rotations/resets agree across servers with no MessagingService and no stored state), RngForSlot(slot, salt), Pick(rng, {{v,w}}) weighted choice, PickDistinct. Cross-phase invariant 3 routes every reset/rotation through Slot(). PURE -- no services, no state, no config reads; the reset-hour knob is MetaConfig.ResetOffsetSec and is passed IN, which is what keeps this Place-neutral. NOTE the `salt` argument on RngForSlot: without it two banners sharing a RotationPeriod would draw the identical featured set forever. GAME DEPLOY PENDING -- deliberately NOT deployed there yet: nothing in the Game reads it until Phase D challenges need Slot(), so the Game reporting MISSING is the EXPECTED state, not drift. Deploy it (and flip deployed.Game) in the session that first needs it.

STORE_NAME stays Beta1_PlayerData(Dev1). Deployed byte-identical (63a0c98a) in GAME (A1) and LOBBY (A2, 2026-08-01) -- drift-green in both Places. Prior hashes: 184cdfad = beta store rename (v1), 8ac5d3e9 = starter-seed removal (v1), 376e717d = original v1. ** SCHEMA v2 -> v3 AT B29 (2026-08-17): adds `BannerChoices`, the Selection banner's per-player stored pick. ** Unblocks blueprint B4's Selection half, which B7 shipped without. Shape is the blueprint's, unchanged: BannerChoices[bannerId] = { TowerId, ChosenAtDay }. ChosenAtDay is a MetaMath.Slot(86400, ResetOffsetSec) DAY NUMBER, NOT a timestamp -- that is what makes Featured.ChoiceCooldown agree across servers with no stored clock (cross-phase invariant 3); the test is currentDay - ChosenAtDay >= cooldownDays. Migrations[2] is a DELIBERATE NO-OP: the key is additive-optional and Reconcile() runs BEFORE Migrate(), so it is already an empty table by then -- but the step must exist because Migrate() WARNS AND STOPS at a missing step, which would strand every later migration. Proven live from a real server Script: a v1 table walks 2 steps to v3, a v2 table walks 1 non-destructively, the live dev profile logged 'Migrated ... forward 1 step(s) to v3' on a real DataStore (DataStoreState=Access), and a written BannerChoices entry SURVIVED a stop/start round trip (8 PASS / 0 FAIL). Deployed to BOTH Places in ONE session per cross-phase invariant 5. NOTE this bump is FORWARD-TOLERANT unlike teleport v4: Reconcile only fills missing keys and never prunes, and Migrate's loop does not run when data.SchemaVersion exceeds a Place's SCHEMA_VERSION -- so a v2 server reading a v3 profile leaves BannerChoices intact rather than destroying it. Publish both anyway. The FLOW (ChooseBannerUnit remote, per-player FeaturedFor, adding Selection to SUPPORTED_TYPES) is AD-Gacha's next session, not this one.

TierConfig.comment: Promoted to shared canon 2026-08-01 (A-phase Integration). RECONCILED from two predecessors: the Game's A3 TierConfig (Order/SortOrder + PascalCase API) and the Lobby's interim TierConfig (multi-colour palettes + ColorSequence helpers, incl. Mythic rainbow / Secret red+dark-red). Every tier authors a Colors LIST; .Color is derived from Colors[1]. Both predecessors are REPLACED. 2026-08-09 (Integration): +SellValueByTier (Silver per tier, blueprint C3 sell-dupes) and GetSellValue(tier), which falls back to 0 -- NOT to Common like GetColor/get -- because this one pays CURRENCY and an unknown tier must never mint Silver. Retune the table, not callers. Prior hash: a0d6e3a3 = the A-phase reconciliation. **490f1f9d -> 7d5850c1 at B27 2026-08-16 (user rule): EVERY TIER NOW HAS AT LEAST TWO COLOURS.** "there should not be a single colored tier ... A Main color and a secondary color, the secondary color is a much darker version of the main color when it only has 1 color." A tier that authors ONE colour gets its second entry DERIVED at load by TierConfig.Darken (HSV: hue and saturation PRESERVED, only VALUE scaled by the single knob SecondaryValueScale = 0.32) and APPENDED into Colors -- so colorSequence/seamlessSequence/isMultiColor are unchanged, every tier animates instead of sitting flat, and there were ZERO call-site changes in either Place. Multi-colour tiers (Mythic's rainbow, Secret's authored red -> dark red) are LEFT EXACTLY AS AUTHORED. GetColor still returns Colors[1], the MAIN colour, so nothing that read .Color moved. Also adds GetSecondaryColor, Luminance and **BrightestColor, which is what a hover stroke is tinted with** -- brightness is RELATIVE LUMINANCE, not HSV value, because by value Mythic's red/orange/blue all tie at 1.0 and the first would win arbitrarily, while by luminance the yellow correctly wins. isMultiColor is now true for every tier; it had no callers outside this module. **7d5850c1 -> 21616fbf at B27c: SecondaryValueScale 0.32 -> 0.62.** The user's verdict on 0.32 was 'the dark is too dark, it should be a SLIGHTLY darker version of its main color'. At 0.32 Rare's secondary was (18,42,82) -- close enough to black that the card read as a fade-to-nothing rather than a two-tone sheen; at 0.62 it is (34,81,158), unmistakably the same blue in shadow. Nothing else moved: still hue+saturation preserved, value scaled. **-> eee2b3ad at B27d: +HoverStrokePaint(tier).** Decides which colours a hover stroke uses: a tier on the two-colour minimum (authored main + derived dark) collapses to the single BrightestColor, because the dark half is just a shadow and a stroke drawn in it reads as a smudge; a tier with THREE OR MORE authored colours returns ALL of them as a ColorSequence, because flattening Mythic's rainbow to one colour throws away the thing that identifies the tier (user rule, B27d). It only DECIDES -- creating/removing the stroke's child UIGradient is UIKitMotion's job, so this module still touches no Instances.

UIKitBootstrap.comment: Kit CONTROLLER (LocalScript, not a ModuleScript -- still hashed as source). Attaches UIKit.Button to every instance tagged 'UIKitButton', including clones added later. Without this in a Place, tagged buttons are inert. Promoted 2026-08-06.

UIKitButton.comment: Kit CONTROLLER. ONE reusable behaviour controller for every GuiButton (hover scale/stroke/icon-rotate, press, seamless animated gradient); all tuning via Attributes. Tag any GuiButton 'UIKitButton' and UIKitBootstrap attaches it. Promoted to shared canon 2026-08-06 with the rest of the kit so the Game place can build on it (blueprint section 9 A6). **4968d8c3 -> 6cc33829 at B27 2026-08-16 (user rule): THE WHOLE BUTTON SCALES ON HOVER/PRESS, NOT JUST ITS CONTENT.** The UIScale moved from `Frame`/`Main` to the ROOT, so the button's own UICorner and UIStroke -- which size themselves from the root -- now travel with the growth instead of staying put while the artwork swelled inside them. Centre-anchoring the root is LAYOUT-SAFE and that was MEASURED, not assumed: a UIGridLayout child and a UIListLayout child were both sampled before and after AnchorPoint = (0.5, 0.5) and NEITHER moved -- a layout overrides the anchor offset when it assigns Position; for a free-positioned button centerAnchor compensates Position itself. Verified live: a card in a UIGridLayout went 150x150 -> 158x158 with its CENTRE unmoved. Any UIScale a template shipped on the inner content is reset to 1 so the two cannot multiply. **6cc33829 -> 9728e897 at B27c.** (1) **THIS IS WHY THE HOTBAR HAD NO VISIBLE HOVER AT ALL:** the controller animated the stroke's Thickness/Transparency but NEVER touched `.Enabled`, and V2's UIHoverStroke ships authored `Enabled = false` -- so on any V2 slot the hover tweened a stroke that was switched off and nothing appeared. A stroke that starts disabled is now DETECTED as hover-only from its authored state (no new Attribute required on every template) and driven. (2) Scales, durations, easing and idle period now DEFER to UIKitMotion.Tuning, so retuning the kit's feel means editing one table; per-button Attributes still override. ** B32 2026-08-19: THE USER'S NEW HUD BUTTON SPEC, plus audio for every button in the project. (1) PANEL-STYLE vs FLAT is DETECTED, NOT CONFIGURED: the new HUD.Left buttons put UICorner+UIHoverStroke on `Main` and leave the ROOT bare (aspect constraint only), while every older button does the opposite. That one difference decides what scales (Main, which honours B27's 'scale the thing that owns the corner and stroke' rule AND is layout-safe for free because the UIListLayout measures the untouched root), how the stroke appears (GROWS from nothing to its authored thickness, vs thickening from a base via HoverStrokeMult), and how its gradient moves (SPINS the Rotation, vs the seamless Offset scroll). `ButtonStyle` overrides it. Detection means zero per-button setup and ZERO behaviour change for the ~48 existing tagged buttons. (2) `LogoContainer` joins the icon lookup AFTER Icon/ButtonImgIcon, so it tilts 45 degrees on hover without changing which instance any existing button rotates. (3) HOVER + CLICK SOUND for every tagged button from ONE place, via UIKit.Sound; per-button `HoverSound`/`ClickSound` attributes, "" to silence. (4) Click = Motion.pressPop, bound on `Activated` so it covers mouse/touch/gamepad and is silent on an inactive button for free. (5) A panel-style hover stroke thinner than 1px WARNS with the instance path and the value -- no number is invented, because the fix is one property in Studio. ** ALSO B32: the `Sound` require is NON-BLOCKING (optionalSibling with a 10s timeout and a no-op stub). A bare WaitForChild on a sibling module blocks FOREVER, and this controller attaches to every tagged button at boot -- so a Place caught mid-deploy would freeze its whole UI instead of merely losing audio. Found exactly that way: Button reached the Game before Sound did and require never returned, hanging the tooling call.

UIKitFilterPanel.comment: Kit CONTROLLER. Reusable filter panel (GroupTemplate + ToggleTemplate + Apply/Reset/Cancel, pending-vs-applied state). Used by BOTH the Units and Items screens in the Lobby. Promoted 2026-08-06.

UIKitHotbar.comment: Kit CONTROLLER. ONE hotbar for BOTH Places so they look and feel identical (user rule 2026-08-06): same slot design, hover, press animation and locked/empty states. Each Place supplies only OnActivated -- Lobby opens the Units screen on that unit, Game starts placement. Always draws LoadoutConfig.MaxSlots slots; a slot is never hidden, only filled/empty/locked. GAME DEPLOY PENDING alongside Kit_HotbarSlot. 2026-08-06 fix: paint BG's OWN UIGradient from the tier too -- only the stroke's gradient was being set, so the slot background stayed at the template's authored red for every unit. BG's gradient and the stroke's gradient are DIFFERENT instances; do not merge the lookups. 2026-08-06: hover preview RESTORED (the first version of this controller dropped the popup the Lobby hotbar used to have). It clones the shared Kit.UnitPreviewTemplate, so both Places pop the same card. Only shown for a FILLED, UNLOCKED slot. B26 2026-08-16: MIGRATED TO Kit.HotbarSlotV2 (prior hash 616b06bf). The old two-surface paint (border stroke + BG's own gradient, and the long comment warning not to confuse them) collapses to ONE root gradient, because V2 has neither instance -- the hazard is deleted, not re-created. Adds UnitLevel (shown only when the entry carries a level, hidden otherwise) and hides PlacementPrice and Placed/MaxPlacement, neither of which has a live data source. 78328bb4 -> baec9162 SAME SESSION, caught by the B26 acceptance run: the UnitLevel write was setText(levelFrame, levelFrame.Name, ...), and setText does root:FindFirstChild(name, true) which walks DESCENDANTS ONLY and never matches root itself -- so it found nothing and left HotbarSlotV2's authored placeholder 'LVL 100' on screen for every unit, in BOTH Places. Now setText(btn, 'UnitLevel', ...) from the slot ROOT. A placeholder rendered as truth is exactly the class of lie section 8 exists to prevent; the assertion that only checked .Visible would never have caught it -- the acceptance harness printing the TEXT is what did. **baec9162 -> 5b8b1609 at B27 2026-08-16 (user rule): the slot's UIHoverStroke is tinted from the tier's BRIGHTEST colour** (TierConfig.BrightestColor, by relative luminance -- Mythic outlines yellow, not its first rainbow entry, and never the derived dark secondary). An EMPTY or LOCKED slot keeps a neutral outline (150,150,165) for exactly the reason its gradient falls back to grey: no unit, no tier. **5b8b1609 -> 69ba6ed1 at B27 2026-08-16: the hover preview's level bar was DEAD.** It read preview:FindFirstChild('UnitLevelBar', true), a name that has never existed on Kit_UnitPreviewTemplate in either Place -- the master shipped that node as 'CanvasGroup' -- so the branch silently did nothing and the preview showed the template's authored placeholder level from B6 onward. B27 renamed the node to EXPLevelBar in both Places and this reads that. No fallback to the old name: nothing ever had it, so a fallback would only preserve the illusion that it once worked. **69ba6ed1 -> f280f1d4 at B27c:** every slot is wrapped by UIKitMotion.isolate, so hovering slot 3 no longer slides slots 4-6 sideways. PlacementPrice is now VISIBLE on a slot that holds a unit -- the TEMPLATE'S AUTHORED placeholder, **not a real cost** (no data source exists in either Place); gated behind Motion.SHOW_PLACEHOLDER_PRICES, the one switch back to hide-never-invent. Empty slots still show no price: a price floating on an empty slot would be noise on top of fiction. **-> dae52036 at B27d:** hover-stroke paint via Motion.paintHoverStroke; an EMPTY or LOCKED slot now also DESTROYS any gradient left by its previous occupant, or the slot keeps outlining as Mythic after the unit leaves. ** B29 2026-08-17: THE HOVER PREVIEW'S HIDE IS NOW OWNED. ** User-reported: "it doesnt show even when mouse is still hovered on the card ... especially when moving fast in between slots and cards." Roblox does NOT guarantee MouseLeave(previous) fires before MouseEnter(next); sweeping the row fast delivers them out of order often enough to see, and the old UNCONDITIONAL hidePreview() then blanked the preview the NEW slot had just shown -- leaving nothing on screen while the mouse sat genuinely hovering a real slot. hidePreview now takes the requesting slot and drops the call when a different slot owns the preview; showPreview claims ownership BEFORE doing any fill work, so a leave from the slot just vacated is already recognisable as stale when it lands. The guard can never strand the preview VISIBLE, because the current owner's own leave still hides normally. A suppressed stale hide prints [DIAG] hotbar hover: suppressed a stale hide -- that line printing IS the race, caught in the act, which is how the bug is proven rather than assumed. The identical defect in the LOBBY-LOCAL UnitsController (card.MouseLeave did hoverPreview.Visible = false unconditionally) was fixed the same way in the same session. The [DIAG] line is THROTTLED (first occurrence, then every 50th): the first instrumented run logged ~70 suppressions in ONE play session, so the race is not occasional -- it is most of a fast sweep, and every one of those would previously have blanked the preview. Unthrottled it buried every other console line.

UIKitItemIcon.comment: Kit CONTROLLER. Item card: flat ImageLabel icon (items have no model, so NO ViewportFrame), QtyBadge that hides at qty 0, tier border/BG from the shared TierConfig. Requires Configs.Meta.{ItemCatalog,TierConfig} -- both already shared. Promoted 2026-08-06. B26 2026-08-16: MIGRATED TO Kit.ItemIconV2 (prior hash b717ebe9). TEMPLATE_PATHS now resolves ItemIconV2; tier paint moved from BG+UIStrokeWithGradient to the ROOT UIGradient (still animated by the SAME shared seamless animator -- do not write a second); IconImage->ItemIcon, QtyBadge->Amount, and the card now fills ItemName. paintStroke() no longer recolours a tier border -- it TOGGLES the authored UIHoverStroke, so hover keeps the same trigger points and feel. **cf5e57cd -> 5cc07ce2 at B27 2026-08-16 (two user rules).** (1) THE WHOLE CARD SCALES: the UIScale moved from `Main` to the ROOT for the same reason as UIKitButton -- UIHoverStroke and UICorner live on the root and were being left behind. (2) THE HOVER STROKE IS TINTED FROM THE TIER'S **BRIGHTEST** COLOUR via TierConfig.BrightestColor, which ranks by RELATIVE LUMINANCE: never Colors[1] (Mythic would outline red for no reason) and never the derived dark secondary (a dark stroke reads as a shadow, not a highlight). **5cc07ce2 -> 81ac91a4 at B27c:** scaling moved onto UIKitMotion.isolate (a fixed-size wrapper, so a hovered card no longer shoves its grid neighbours), hover/press now use the kit's single Quint curve, the idle gradient runs through Motion (45 degrees, 9s instead of 3s), the card LIFTS above its neighbours while hovered, and destroy() takes the wrapper with it so rebuilds cannot leave empty slots padding the grid. **-> cf4d9eda at B27d:** hover-stroke paint is now one Motion.paintHoverStroke call (3+-colour tiers outline in all their colours).

Kit_UnitIconV2.comment: Kit TEMPLATE, the USER's V2 unit card. ADOPTED at B26 2026-08-16, REPLACING Kit_UnitIcon outright (that row is retired, the B2 RewardPopup precedent). No shared/src file -- the INSTANCE is canon (ADR-0005); copy it between Places and verify by hash, never rebuild by hand. *** RARITY IS PAINTED ON THE ROOT UIGradient AND THERE IS NO TIER BORDER *** (user decision, B25): v1's BG fill + UIStrokeWithGradient border do not exist here, and UIHoverStroke is HOVER-ONLY (authored Enabled=false, driven from MouseEnter/MouseLeave). Every consumer looks up the root gradient with FindFirstChildOfClass -- DIRECT CHILDREN ONLY, because V2 nests UIGradients under UnitLevel/PlacementPrice/TraitIcon and a recursive find repaints the wrong one. THREE consumers: SummonController featured chips, IndexController codex entries, and AscensionController's dupe picker (the third was missed by earlier notes -- it reads UnitLevel). Renames from v1: NameLabel->UnitName, LevelBadge->UnitLevel, CostLabel->PlacementPrice, CountLabel stays but is now a TextLabel not a Frame. B26 AUTHORED CountLabel (user-delegated): v1's was a Frame while IndexController guards on IsA('TextLabel'), so the owned-count had NEVER rendered; V2's is a real TextLabel and the branch is finally live. NO ShinyBadge (v1 had one, AscensionController drove it) -- shiny is not marked on a V2 card. PlacementPrice/ElementIcons/TraitIcon render HIDDEN: they have NO data source (AD-Game + AD-Traits proposals). **-> at B27d: `Active` flipped false -> TRUE.** The master shipped `Active = false`, and `GuiButton.Activated` DOES NOT FIRE on an inactive button -- so every `Activated` connection on a V2 card has been dead since the B26 adoption: the Units grid, IndexController's detail open, AscensionController's dupe picker, UIKit.ItemIcon's onActivated (the Items grid) and BOTH hotbars' slot activation, which in the GAME means placement. Reported by the user as 'the units gui click selection is not working'; confirmed by GetGuiObjectsAtPosition showing nothing covering the card and the card itself reading Active=false. UIKitButton.setEnabled still drives Active per-slot, so locked hotbar slots stay genuinely unclickable. ** B32 2026-08-19: +Main.SelectedToSellOverlay (ImageLabel), the user's 'this one is going' marker for the multi-select sell flow. 0bf1a11e -> bf39c6c8. The user authored it on UnitsGUI.Main.Bottom.UnitsContainer.UnitIconV2, which is DESIGN SCAFFOLDING the controller destroys at boot -- so it had to move into the shared master to reach real cards. Built in BOTH Places by the SAME deterministic script and hash-matched, which is the second of the two routes templatesNote sanctions. TWO deliberate changes from what was authored: Visible FALSE (the template must not ship every card looking already selected) and ZIndex 20 rather than 1 (at 1 it drew UNDER TraitIcon at 10, CountLabel at 5 and the flag strip at 2, so it could not cover the card it exists to cover).

NOTE ObtainRewardsController's paintTier deliberately handles BOTH shapes -- it also paints the user's Lobby-local UnitTemplate, which is still v1-shaped and was NOT part of this migration. **-> at B27d: `Active` flipped false -> TRUE.** The master shipped `Active = false`, and `GuiButton.Activated` DOES NOT FIRE on an inactive button -- so every `Activated` connection on a V2 card has been dead since the B26 adoption: the Units grid, IndexController's detail open, AscensionController's dupe picker, UIKit.ItemIcon's onActivated (the Items grid) and BOTH hotbars' slot activation, which in the GAME means placement. 'Placed/MaxPlacement' is a MATCH-runtime count: nothing feeds it yet so it is hidden in both; NOTE the '/' in its instance name means FindFirstChild, never dot notation. **-> at B27d: `Active` flipped false -> TRUE.** The master shipped `Active = false`, and `GuiButton.Activated` DOES NOT FIRE on an inactive button -- so every `Activated` connection on a V2 card has been dead since the B26 adoption: the Units grid, IndexController's detail open, AscensionController's dupe picker, UIKit.ItemIcon's onActivated (the Items grid) and BOTH hotbars' slot activation, which in the GAME means placement. Reported by the user as 'the units gui click selection is not working'; confirmed by GetGuiObjectsAtPosition showing nothing covering the card and the card itself reading Active=false. UIKitButton.setEnabled still drives Active per-slot, so locked hotbar slots stay genuinely unclickable. *** CROSS-PLACE DRIFT RESOLVED AT B28 (2026-08-17), LOBBY CANONICAL BY USER DECISION. *** B27d had recorded the two Places disagreeing (Lobby cd5a2aa0, Game 9ca7a958) on two properties. At B28 both were re-measured in Studio before any write, and only ONE of the two was still real: root `Size` was {1,0},{1,0} in the Lobby and {0.225,0},{0.399,0} in the Game. `UIHoverStroke.Thickness` ALREADY READ 0.035 IN BOTH -- B27d's '0.0 in the Game' no longer held, so nothing was written to it; the value was asserted, not set. The Game's Size was set to {1,0},{1,0} by deterministic edit (checklists.md step 2's exception path -- cheaper and safer than a cross-Place copy, and the same route the B27b CanvasGroup rename took), and BOTH Places then hashed cd5a2aa0. Why {1,1} is safe in the Game: `UIKit.Hotbar.attach` CLONES this master MaxSlots times and never overrides Size, both Places' `StarterGui.Hotbar.Slots` containers are the identical {0.420723,0},{0.157785,0} Frame under a horizontal UIListLayout, and the master carries a UIAspectRatioConstraint (ratio 1.0034, FitWithinMaxSize, Width) which is what actually clamps the slot -- so {1,1} resolves to the same square the Lobby already draws. The Game's authored Slot1..Slot6 in StarterGui are destroyed and re-cloned by attach(), so they do not need editing.

UIKitMotion.comment: Kit CONTROLLER (motion). ADDED B27c 2026-08-16. ONE home for how the kit MOVES: hover/press scaling, the idle gradient drift, and the tuning numbers behind both -- four screens plus three kit controllers had each grown their own copy of the same three effects with three different durations. **THE HEADLINE IS `isolate()`: a UIScale on a child of a UIListLayout/UIGridLayout CHANGES THAT CHILD'S MEASURED SIZE, so hovering one card re-flows the layout and every sibling slides.** Measured, not assumed: a 150px card at scale 1.2 under a horizontal UIListLayout shoved its neighbour 30px. isolate() puts a FIXED-SIZE wrapper between the layout and the card and moves the UIScale onto the card inside it -- same measurement then moved the neighbour 0px while the card still grew 150->195. The wrapper must never set ClipsDescendants (it would crop the growth it exists to allow) and it CLONES the card's UIAspectRatioConstraint/UISizeConstraint -- without that a 175x175 card produced a 175x405 slot and every card floated in vertical dead space. Because the wrapper is what the layout sees, visibility and layout order must go through Motion.setVisible / setLayoutOrder, and disposal through Motion.destroy, or filtered-out cards leave empty slots padding the row. Also owns Tuning (Quint ease-out; hover 0.26s, press 0.09s, rest 0.30s -- rest is slowest so nothing snaps back; idle period 9s, up from a jittery 3s; gradient Rotation 45 per the user) and lift(), which raises a hovered card's ZIndex so its growth is never drawn underneath the sibling after it. **CARRIES ONE TEMPORARY FLAG THAT IS NOT A MOTION CONCERN: SHOW_PLACEHOLDER_PRICES.** The standing rule is HIDE, NEVER INVENT; the user explicitly suspended it for testing ('show the prices for now ... just to see it visually'). PlacementPrice therefore renders the TEMPLATE'S AUTHORED value, which is a design placeholder and NOT a real cost -- no Lobby data source for placement cost exists. It is parked here because every card consumer already requires Motion, so this is the single switch that flips all of them back to honest. **-> ed800bf3 at B27d: +paintHoverStroke(stroke, tier)**, the Instance half of TierConfig.HoverStrokePaint. Two traps it handles: stroke.Color is forced to WHITE in the gradient case because a UIStroke MULTIPLIES its Color with a child UIGradient (leaving the tier colour would tint the whole rainbow), and a stale gradient is DESTROYED when a tier falls back to two colours, or a card recycled from Mythic to Rare keeps outlining in rainbow forever. ** B28 2026-08-17: ADDS THE OPEN/CLOSE SLIDE ** (`slideIn`/`slideOut`/`isOpen`/`restPosition`/`forgetSlide`, plus Tuning.SlideInTime 0.34 / SlideOutTime 0.20 / SlideDistance 0.35). Last item of the user's B27 queue: "I also need animations when opening in closing, Like sliding up, not just popping visible and invisible." It is HERE and not in the screens for the same reason hover is -- a fourth animation dialect is what this module exists to prevent. Three traps are handled once, so no screen repeats them: (1) every screen toggles ScreenGui.Enabled and a DISABLED ScreenGui does not lay out (everything under it reads AbsoluteSize 0), so slideIn ENABLES BEFORE touching Position and slideOut DISABLES ONLY AFTER the close tween completes; (2) travel is PARENT-RELATIVE SCALE, never measured pixels -- a measured slide would have to wait a frame for AbsoluteSize to go non-zero, and 'a harness reporting 0x0 is usually the harness' is this project's most repeated false alarm; (3) the designer's authored resting Position is captured ONCE into the `UIKitRestPosition` attribute (UDim2 is a real attribute type, so it is visible in Studio and survives a reload) and every tween runs to or from THAT -- no screen coordinate is hardcoded. Re-entrancy is a per-frame token: a completion callback holding a stale token does nothing, which is what stops a late slideOut from disabling a gui the user has already reopened. Deployed to BOTH Places in one session and hash-matched against shared/src byte-for-byte (18485 bytes). ** B32 2026-08-19: +spinGradient/stopSpin (UIGradient.Rotation looped forever -- the idle animation for a BORDER, where idleGradient's Offset scroll is the one for a card FACE; the base Rotation is stored in the `UIKitBaseRotation` attribute for the same reason UIKitRestPosition is, and it is idempotent so a controller re-running on every hover cannot stack tweens), +growStroke (Thickness 0<->target, and it OWNS .Enabled -- enabled BEFORE growing, disabled only AFTER shrinking, because a DISABLED UIStroke tweening Thickness animates nothing at all, which is the B27c hotbar bug; Thickness is zeroed only when the stroke was actually off so re-hovering mid-shrink grows from where it got to), +pressPop (dip -> Back/Out overshoot -> hand control back via onComplete; it shares activeScaleTweens with scaleTo so a click and a hover cannot fight over one UIScale, and it deliberately does NOT guess where to land because by the time a click finishes the button may have closed the screen it lived on). Tuning gains StrokeGrowTime 0.22, GradientSpinPeriod 4, ClickDip/Pop/Settle.

UIKitSound.comment: Kit CONTROLLER (audio). ADDED B32 2026-08-19 (owner AD-UI). ONE home for UI one-shots, gameplay SFX and music. *** ASSIGNING A SOUND IS PASTING AN ID IN STUDIO -- THERE IS NO CONFIG FILE. *** Every sound is a real `Sound` instance under SoundService in a folder named after its category (UI / SFX / BGM) and this module resolves it BY NAME, so adding or retuning one is never a code change in either Place. To give a stage its own music, name a Sound EXACTLY the act id (Stage1_Act1, ...); playBGM falls back to `BGM.Default`, so an unnamed stage is silent rather than broken. Instances rather than a config table because a Sound carries Volume/Looped/TimePosition/PlaybackSpeed as AUTHORED properties a designer can hear while tuning, and a table would separate the ids from the volumes. SoundGroups (Master > UI/SFX/BGM) because one Volume per category is exactly what the PENDING unified settings screen needs and the only way to duck music under SFX later without touching every Sound. THIS IS A CLIENT MODULE: playing a Sound on the server plays it for nobody in particular. Degrades quietly by design -- a missing NAME warns once and no-ops, while an EMPTY SoundId is 'not assigned yet' (the normal state of a fresh project) and is reported once at boot by Sound.report() as a list instead of warning on every click. The authored Volume is captured into the `UIKitBaseVolume` attribute, same reasoning as Motion's UIKitRestPosition. Music crossfades (out 0.8s faster than in 1.6s: a gap between tracks reads as a bug, overlap reads as a transition) and re-requesting the playing track is a NO-OP so a screen calling playBGM on every open cannot restart the music.

UIKitConfirm.comment: Kit CONTROLLER (confirmation dialog). ADDED B32 2026-08-19 (owner AD-UI), at the user's request to 'use it globally even in game place'. SHARED because 'are you sure?' is asked by things with nothing else in common -- selling units, leaving a match, spending premium currency, resetting settings -- and every one of those growing its own popup is how four dialogs end up with four button orders and three meanings for the greyed-out state. The DESIGN is the authored ScreenGui StarterGui.ConfirmationPopupUI (Background > ConfirmationFrame > Main > ConfirmationLabel/ConfirmationText/YesButton/NoButton); this module is only the behaviour. *** THE ASK IS A YIELDING FUNCTION CALL that returns a boolean *** (`if Confirm.ask{...} then`), so a caller reads top-to-bottom instead of splitting across two callbacks; every screen here already does its remote work inside task.spawn so the yield costs them nothing. THE TWO-SECOND GATE IS THE POINT: YesButton starts GREY and inactive, counts down in its own ButtonText, then turns GREEN and becomes clickable -- a deliberate speed bump on irreversible actions, because B31's sell path destroys units permanently and muscle memory must not be able to carry a player through it. NoButton is live immediately: backing out is never the dangerous direction. Re-entrancy is refused rather than queued (two stacked prompts is how a player answers the wrong one) and EVERY failure path returns FALSE, because the safe answer to a question nobody could see is no. B32 also renamed the two authored buttons: they were BOTH called `SellButton` (duplicate names make dot access pick an arbitrary one) and were identified by their ButtonText to become YesButton/NoButton. ScreenGui DisplayOrder raised 10 -> 100 so it draws above PartyScreen (30). Parts resolve FRESH on every ask because the ScreenGui is ResetOnSpawn. ** Its Motion/Sound requires are NON-BLOCKING for the same reason as UIKitButton's, with a degraded Motion stub that shows and hides the frame without the slide.

UIKitNotify.comment: Kit CONTROLLER (toast notifications). PROMOTED TO SHARED CANON B34 2026-08-20 (owner AD-UI). The GAME grew this first as Client.UI.NotificationController, used by PlacementController and TowerSelectionUI. At B33 the user copied it into the LOBBY and asked for it Lobby-wide, which left TWO copies in DIFFERENT paths in NEITHER manifest, and only the Lobby's hardened -- a fork with no drift control, which is the exact failure the shared-canon system exists to prevent. Both copies are RETIRED (renamed *_RETIRED_2026-08-20, per the Hotbar_RETIRED convention) and all five consumers (Lobby: UnitsController/SummonController/AscensionController; Game: PlacementController/TowerSelectionUI) now require this. The API is unchanged -- Error/Success/Warning/Info(msg) and Notify(msg, kind) -- so repointing was ONE line per consumer and the ~20 call sites were untouched. *** SAME SPLIT AS UIKitConfirm: the MODULE is canon, the GUI it drives (StarterGui.Notifications -- Container + CardTemplate) stays PER-PLACE AUTHORED ART, because art cannot be scripted and copying a ScreenGui between Places is a USER action (B26). *** THE RULE FOR CALLERS IS `TOAST EVENTS, LABEL STATE`: a card self-dismisses after Tuning.Duration (3.5s), which is right for something that HAPPENED and WRONG for something that IS TRUE -- erasing a still-current condition after 3.5s is worse than never showing it, so persistent state stays on a label. CLIENT module: a server require warns and degrades to print-only rather than erroring, because a misplaced require should cost a toast and never a boot. All internal lookups are BOUNDED (the B33 lesson -- a bare WaitForChild in a module required by screen controllers stops being 'no toasts' and becomes 'that screen never finishes booting'); a missing GUI disables toasts, prints instead, and affects no screen. Tuning{Duration,MaxCards,PopTime,FadeTime,PopFrom,FadeToScale} is the one place to retune feel; Colors is the kind->Color3 map; IsAvailable() reports whether toasts will actually appear here.

UIKitUnitCard.comment: Kit CONTROLLER (unit-card presentation). ADDED B34 2026-08-20 (owner AD-UI). The two things every screen showing a Kit.UnitIconV2 had to do for itself: frame a model in a ViewportFrame, and paint the card in its tier's colours. FOUR screens each carried their own copy -- Units, Summon, Index, Ascension -- and it was MEASURED before extracting rather than assumed: `setViewportModel` was BYTE-IDENTICAL across Summon/Index/Ascension and Units differed in exactly ONE way, the SOURCE of the model (its own `modelFor` helper for ascended forms instead of an inline clone); `paintTier` was again byte-identical across those three, with Units additionally running the idle sheen and forcing the hover stroke off. So viewport() takes the MODEL (the caller keeps the difference that was real) and paintTier() takes {Idle, StrokeOff} (the two behaviours that were real). Everything else merged exactly. FOUR copies of a camera-framing formula is four places for it to drift, and the drift would be SILENT -- a card framed slightly differently on one screen reads as an art bug nobody files. Framing{FieldOfView=40, DistancePadding=1.3, DistanceBias=2, HeightFraction=0.05} is the one place to retune it; the bias exists so a TINY model does not end up with the camera inside it. viewport() CLEARS the WorldModel unconditionally BEFORE the nil check, or a recycled card keeps showing the previous unit. paintTier's UIGradient lookup is DIRECT-CHILD on purpose and must stay one: V2 nests further UIGradients under UnitLevel/PlacementPrice/TraitIcon and a recursive find would repaint one of those instead of the card. CLIENT module, owns no state. Deployed to BOTH Places for kit uniformity even though all four consumers are currently Lobby-side. Dependencies (Motion, TierConfig) load through BOUNDED lookups -- the B32/B33 lesson: a bare WaitForChild in a module required by screen controllers stops being 'this feature is missing' and becomes 'that screen never finishes booting', with no error to read.

SettingsConfig.comment: PROMOTED TO SHARED CANON B35 2026-08-20 (owner AD-Game, schema shared with AD-UI). The one structure behind the unified settings system the user asked for: 'there will be one settings system for both game and lobby ... but both should use same structure, same gui.' Two fields carry that: Scope (Both/GameOnly/LobbyOnly) decides where an entry is SHOWN, Kind (Preference/Action) decides whether it PERSISTS. A Place difference is therefore a config field and NEVER a branch in a script -- SettingsUI contains no Place-specific `if` at all. *** THE TRAP, AND THE REASON Sanitize IGNORES Scope: one profile serves BOTH Places. If Sanitize dropped out-of-scope keys, changing any setting in the Lobby would sanitize every GameOnly preference out of the payload and PERMANENTLY LOSE it (and vice versa). So Sanitize processes every Preference regardless of Scope; Scope is a rendering concern only. Proven live at B35: a Game-side save left the LobbyOnly SkipRevealAnim intact, and MusicVolume set in the Game was read back in the Lobby. *** Actions have no Default and are skipped by Sanitize entirely, so a button press can never persist as a preference. KEY-NAME NOTE: `SoundVolume` IS the SFX slider -- do NOT rename it to SFXVolume; it shipped as the only volume key and players have saved values under it, so a rename silently resets everyone. Place() is the ONE definition of the Workspace.Lobby assertion every script in the project otherwise repeats. NO save-schema bump was needed: Data.Settings has been free-form {[string]: any} since v1.

SettingsService.comment: PROMOTED TO SHARED CANON B35 2026-08-20 (owner AD-Game). The server side of settings: profile-backed, Sanitize as the trust boundary before any write, persistence riding ProfileStore's session autosave. ONE profile serves both Places, so two independently-written services would eventually sanitize differently and each quietly clobber the other's keys -- which is the whole argument for promoting it. The only change promotion required was the PlayerDataService require: it was `script.Parent.Parent.Data.PlayerDataService`, a RELATIVE path that only resolves in the Game's folder layout; it is now absolute and resolves in both Places because PlayerDataService is itself canon at a fixed path. *** THE REMOTE WAITS FOR THE PROFILE (WaitForData, 20s) AND THAT IS NOT OPTIONAL. *** The client fetches once at boot and caches the answer for the whole session; without the wait that fetch lands before ProfileStore finishes loading, Get() falls through to Sanitize(nil) = DEFAULTS, and the player spends the session with real settings on the server and default ones on screen -- experienced as 'my settings reset every time I join', with nothing in the log to explain it. Caught live at B35 in the Lobby: the server held MusicVolume 0.25 while the BGM SoundGroup sat at the 0.5 default.

ClientSettings.comment: PROMOTED TO SHARED CANON B35 2026-08-20 (owner AD-Game). One in-memory home for the local player's settings, with a Changed signal every client system subscribes to. *** THE DEPLOY PATH DELIBERATELY DID NOT MOVE: *** five Game scripts require it as `script.Parent.Parent.Settings.ClientSettings`, so keeping the path identical in both Places made promotion cost ZERO consumer edits -- the Lobby simply grew the same Client/Settings folders. Moving it to Shared would have been tidier and would have meant editing five working files in another owner's Place for no behaviour change. *** FIXES A REAL DEAD SLIDER: *** the old code drove a SoundGroup called `MasterSFX`, which has never existed in either Place, so the volume setting controlled precisely nothing. It now drives the B32 groups (SoundService.Groups.Master > UI/SFX/BGM) with one slider each for Music/SFX/UI; a missing group is skipped rather than created, because inventing audio routing behind the player's back is worse than a slider that visibly does nothing. Also owns the ACTION registry (RegisterAction/HasAction/RunAction): an action is the one part of settings that genuinely differs per Place, so the config DECLARES actions and each Place SUPPLIES behaviour; unregistered actions render disabled instead of pretending. RunAction spawns the handler so a yielding action cannot block the click and an erroring one cannot take the panel down.

SettingsUI.comment: PROMOTED TO SHARED CANON B35 2026-08-20 (owner AD-UI). LocalScript, hashed as source -- same precedent as UIKitBootstrap. ONE screen builder for both Places: it asks SettingsConfig what is in scope and draws exactly that, so there is NO Place-specific branch anywhere in the file (Game renders 11 rows / 5 tabs, Lobby renders 6 rows -- verified live at B35). Rows are cloned from the authored templates, so adding a setting stays a config edit. THE GUI IS PER-PLACE AUTHORED ART: StarterGui.Settings is NOT canon, because copying a ScreenGui between Places is a USER action (B26) -- so this script degrades to one clear warning and stands down when the art is not there yet, which is exactly the Lobby's state until the user copies it across. Action buttons repaint on every OPEN, not just at build: handlers are registered by separate scripts and LocalScript run order is not guaranteed, so a build-time-only paint would show N/A forever whenever the registrar happened to run second. Two syntax lessons are baked into the file's comments after they took it down on first deploy: a statement beginning with `(` parses as a call to the previous line (Luau: 'ambiguous syntax'), and a leading `;` is not a legal way to start a block in Luau at all -- both are avoided by binding typed locals once.

templatesNote: Templates are under drift control since 2026-08-06 (ADR-0005). They have NO shared/src file: the Instance is the canon. Two safe ways to get one into another Place: COPY it (Studio copy/paste) and prove equality by hash, OR build it with an identical DETERMINISTIC script run in both Places and hash-match (used for Kit_UnitIcon). Never rebuild by hand/by eye. See tools/checklists.md.
